MATCH (d:Person)-[:DIRECTED]->(m:Movie)

MATCH (a:Person)-[:ACTED_IN]->(m)

Career at a Glance (International)

Kohli's international career, spanning over 15 years, is characterized by incredible consistency, an insatiable hunger for runs, and unparalleled success in run-chases. He is part of an elite group of players who have dominated all three formats of the game simultaneously, holding numerous records for the fastest to achieve run milestones.

His aggregate numbers place him among the absolute pantheon of cricketing greats, alongside names like Sachin Tendulkar, Ricky Ponting, and Jacques Kallis. He holds the record for the most centuries in One Day International cricket and stands as the highest run-scorer in T20 Internationals.

Conclusion and Legacy

Virat Kohli's legacy in cricket transcends mere statistics. While his numbers-over 26,000 international runs, 80 centuries, and an average hovering near 50 across all formats-secure his place in the statistical hall of fame, his true impact lies in his intensity.

He redefined fitness standards in cricket, transforming the Indian team into a squad of elite athletes capable of competing intensely in the field for five grueling days. His aggressive body language and unwavering self-belief eradicated the traditional, submissive stereotype sometimes associated with subcontinental touring teams.

The Final Verdict

Whether navigating a tricky run-chase under the lights in an ODI, battling hostile fast bowling on a green pitch in England, or orchestrating a Test match victory as an animated captain, Kohli has given modern cricket some of its most iconic and enduring memories. He is, unequivocally, a generational talent whose records will stand as benchmarks for decades to come.
